content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (critical rule IP).**

**What the document says.** Ownership is addressed in two places:
- **§2.8 (p0043)** — Commerce One retains all rights in the Software, licensed not sold. This is fine; a vendor keeping its platform is expressly acceptable under the rule.
- **§13.5 (p0115–p0116)** — Developments (interface coding/programs created solely by Corio to make the Software run in the Corio hosted environment) are owned by Corio, and Commerce One assigns any claim it would otherwise have. Good so far, and the vendor also warrants employee invention-assignment agreements.

**Why it fails.** §13.5 contains a carve-out: where a Development "[is] supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One," Commerce One "will retain all ownership rights, including intellectual property rights in the Developments" — with no licence back. That flips ownership of IP we created and paid for to the vendor, which is walk-away territory, and it also fails the fallback because Corio is left with no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free right to use or modify its own integration code.

**Redline (validated ok:true).** Smallest edit to reach the preferred position: delete only the carve-out clause in p0115 and the orphaned fragment carrying it over in p0116. Commerce One's pre-existing materials and the Software remain its property.

**Noted, not flagged separately:** no express Customer Data / hosted data ownership statement anywhere in the agreement, and the last sentence of §13.5 leaves ownership of enhancements to the Software itself to future negotiation. Both are drafting points to raise if §13 is reopened, not independent breaches.
